newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Uzbekistan sees better cotton harvest in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Uzbekistan sees better cotton harvest in 1997.

text.p: Uzbekistan, one of the world's largest producers and exporters of cotton, hopes that due to better weather conditions this year's harvest of raw cotton will be higher than last year's 3.35 million tonnes.

"Sowing of cotton has been successfully completed, and 85 percent of the total sown area has given qualitative shoots which is 10 percent more than last year," an agriculture ministry official told Reuters by phone from the capital Tashkent.
He said good weather conditions in April and timely sowing were the main prerequisites of a possibly higher cotton crop this year.
Cotton was sown this year on 1.5 million hectares, the same as last year, and the government has set a plan to grow a total four million tonnes of raw cotton, unchanged from the 1996 plan.
Farmers gathered only 3.35 million tonnes last year due to a colder than usual spring and a rainy autumn, but the official said this year's harvest was likely to be higher.

According to estimates from the International Cotton Advisory Committee, in 1995 Uzbekistan was the world's fifth producer of cotton fibre with 1.25 million tonnes and its second largest exporter with 1.05 million tonnes. It harvested 3.93 million tonnes of raw cotton in 1995.
